headline: US now requires export licenses for overseas compute serving Chinese companies, reshaping AI infrastructure
dek: A new Commerce rule issued Monday licenses remote access to advanced chips worldwide and adds license requirements for five fast-growing data center markets. Chip stocks fell 4.6% ahead of Nvidia's results tonight.

asks.text: portfolio and pipeline exposure to the remote-access rule, including whether "digitally-linked infrastructure" covers decentralized GPU networks
whether AI infrastructure term sheets under negotiation should add export-control representations and customer-checking requirements
what Nvidia's results, the reported Anthropic IPO and a priced-in December hike mean for AI round pricing and crypto underwriting
which of our biotech companies fit Lilly's and J&J's current acquisition patterns

sections.name: AI Systems
sections.thesis: Compute access is now a licensed, know-your-customer business, and US hyperscalers hold the advantage.

items.title: BIS interim final rule requires licenses for overseas data centers giving Chinese companies large-scale compute access
items.why: data centers must now know their customers' ultimate owners, the US-headquartered exemption favors US hyperscalers in Malaysia, Singapore and Brazil, and "linked data centers" explicitly includes digitally-linked infrastructure that could reach decentralized GPU networks.
items.watch: Federal Register publication, which agency leads enforcement, and the 60-day comment window.
items.source_note: Threshold is 12M aggregate TPP (about 760 H100s per a third-party estimate); new license requirement for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil; rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule. Decentralized-network reading is our interpretation, not legal advice.

items.title: Anthropic IPO reportedly expected later this week
items.why: alongside Nvidia's results, it would set the public-market price for frontier AI labs.
items.source_note: single mention in one Reuters markets story; no terms seen

items.title: Noeri, founded by Stanford's Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, raises $110M led by Menlo Ventures
items.why: money is flowing into the layer that makes cheaper models do the job of frontier models, with the pitch built on cost per task rather than model size.
items.watch: customer data on cost per task versus frontier models.
items.source_note: cites company and Bloomberg; valuation not disclosed

also_noted: Nvidia reports Q3 after the close today, its first under interim CEO Colette Kress; analysts expect about $109.1B in revenue (Reuters).
Monday: Nvidia -4.2%, CoreWeave -6.2%, Nebius -7.5%; Nasdaq -2.3% and in correction.
Nvidia launched Nemotron for Science plus an open chemistry dataset of about 50K questions (company release).

sections.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
sections.thesis: Bitcoin is trading as a risk asset in the AI sell-off while a sanctioned economy opens retail access.

items.title: Bank of Russia opens BTC, ETH and USDT to non-qualified retail investors from Nov 17
items.why: a large sanctioned economy now has regulated retail access with USDT as the only listed stablecoin, raising compliance questions for USDT-exposed businesses under the GENIUS Act.
items.watch: purchase volumes and responses from Tether and US or EU regulators.
items.source_note: secondhand; Bank of Russia text not reviewed

items.title: Bitcoin near $65K, down about 13–14% on the week, as Strategy faces an estimated $2.8B in MSCI index selling
items.why: bitcoin is moving with AI stocks rather than hedging them, and Strategy's Nov 30 MSCI removal tests the crypto-treasury company model.
items.watch: Fed minutes Nov 18 and the Nov 30 MSCI rebalance.
items.source_note: $2.8B selling figure is a JPMorgan estimate

also_noted: Spot Bitcoin ETFs: seven straight days of outflows, about $2.1B in November (Cryptonomist).
Markets price a 93.7% chance of a December Fed rate hike (Reuters, CME FedWatch).
Bullish and CoinShares report earnings Nov 18.

sections.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
sections.thesis: Big pharma keeps buying early, paying up for assets before human trials.

items.title: Lilly to buy preclinical blood cancer biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B, its 14th acquisition of 2026
items.why: paying up to $1.5B for a preclinical antibody supports early-exit planning for preclinical biotechs.
items.watch: deal terms and whether other pharmas follow with preclinical buys.
items.source_note: single source, paywalled; seen in search snippet

items.title: J&J to acquire eye disease company Ollin Biosciences for $2.2B upfront plus up to $1.1B in milestones
items.why: large-pharma demand for clinical-stage ophthalmology assets remains steady.
items.watch: closing timeline and other ophthalmology deals.
items.source_note: company announcement via trade press; full page not accessed

also_noted: FDA approved Novartis's Cosentyx for polymyalgia rheumatica, first anti-IL-17 for the condition (company release).
Remedy Robotics raised a $62M Series B led by DCVC for intravascular robotics (single source, funding database).

sections.name: Deep Tech
sections.thesis: Quantum is being sold as a supercomputer add-on; the value is in the integration software.

items.title: IBM, Fermilab and Nvidia push quantum-HPC integration at SC26
items.why: near-term value sits in software connecting quantum processors to existing supercomputer workflows, not qubit counts alone.
items.watch: general availability of quantum job scheduling in Slurm, due late November.
items.source_note: company claims; IBM says Nighthawk r2 runs up to 100K samples/sec, 25x Heron

also_noted: Silex Microsystems to invest $131.4M in its first US MEMS factory in Mountain Top, Pennsylvania.
TSMC stock down 9.7% in three days despite record October revenue of about NT$587B.

sections.name: Robotics & Autonomy
sections.thesis: Factory-built robotaxis are reaching paid driverless service.

items.title: Pony.ai and Toyota launch fully driverless paid rides in mass-produced bZ4X robotaxis in Guangzhou
items.why: a global carmaker's assembly-line vehicle now carries paying passengers with no driver, moving robotaxis past retrofits.
items.watch: fleet count, new cities and cost per vehicle.
items.source_note: company source; no fleet size or unit economics disclosed
